summary: Local retailers are blending in-store and online shopping through omnichannel strategies, covering synchronized inventory, local e-commerce platforms, social commerce, personalized marketing, customer experience investment and staff training. Local business owners and a consultant describe concrete results, and a Local Commerce Coalition study links cohesive omnichannel experiences to higher customer retention. The article argues this shift is reshaping local economies and defining the future of retail.
one_line: Local retailers are adopting omnichannel strategies that merge physical and online shopping, boosting retention, sales and customer engagement in local economies.
key_facts: A Local Commerce Coalition study released on October 13, 2023 found a 30% increase in customer retention rates for businesses offering a cohesive omnichannel experience.
Sarah McIntyre of McIntyre's Homewares said on September 10, 2023 that customers don't differentiate between a store and an online platform.
Bill Harmon of Harmon's Electronics has had a system since November 1, 2023 that synchronizes in-store and online inventories.
Tammy Rodriguez of Rodriguez Fashion Boutique launched an online storefront in late September 2023 and now sells to customers nationwide.
Michelle Avery, who runs a small artisanal cheese shop, uses Instagram Stories and the shopping feature so customers can buy cheeses right away.

Chris Thompson of Thompson's Bookstore sends personalized reading suggestions based on purchase history and browsing behavior, and shared his increased engagement and sales at a local business conference on January 15, 2024.

Julia Peterson revamped Peterson's Pantry with interactive in-store cooking demonstrations also streamed online, and said on February 5, 2024 that it bridged the gap between in-person and online engagement.
Retail consultant Lance Donovan stated at a retail technology forum on March 21, 2024 that investment in personnel is just as important as investment in technology.
Local retailers are forming partnerships with web developers and digital marketers to build online platforms reflecting their store ethos.
Local retailers are implementing software that provides real-time stock updates across all selling channels.
The article says local e-commerce expansion is a strategic complement to in-person shopping, not merely an attempt to mimic giants like Amazon.
